summary: A whole comparison screen from data: two to four options (plans, phones, laptops) on the same rows, each option a card with its name, price and a Choose button. From the width where every column fits (about 150 dp each, 440 to 760 dp wide) a real table: the options as columns beside a column of row labels, values aligned, the featured option tinted with a Most popular badge, the header kept while the rows scroll. Narrower, two options side by side on the same rows, each side with a picker that steps to another option; it opens on the featured one and its neighbour. Choose highlights the option with a ring and sends its index to the host.

options.doc: 2 to 4 objects: {"name", "price", "period", "note", "badge", "values"}, all but name and values optional. name (Pro, Pixel 10) one line; price a short string ("€9.99", "$799", "Free"); period after it, small ("/month"); note two short lines under it ("For one person"); badge a chip over the name ("Best value"; badges show only when featured is set, which reserves their row). values: one per row, in the order of rows: a string ("128 GB", "4K"), true (a tick), false (a cross) or null (a dash). Numbers must be strings: "2", not 2

rows.doc: The attributes compared, in order: strings ("Screens", "Battery") or {"label"}. Up to two lines in the table's label column, one line as a caption on a phone

title.doc: The heading ("Choose your plan"): the table's top-left corner when wide, a 56 dp row on a phone (dropped when the window is short)

subtitle.doc: A short line under the title, in the corner of the table only ("Cancel any time")

featured.doc: The highlighted option, from 0: its column is tinted, it gets featuredLabel as a badge (unless it has its own), and a phone opens on it and its neighbour. -1: none

selected.doc: The chosen option, from 0, -1 for none yet. Choose sets it and its card gets a ring and a filled Selected button. Bind a resources variable ("@plan") to preset or read it. Do not name it step

action.doc: The host action every Choose and Selected button sends, with the option's index as a float value

rowHeight.doc: A table row's height when wide; a phone's rows are 60 (a caption and two lines)

colMin.doc: Narrowest option column of the table; the table shows from labelMin + n x colMin + 32 dp

colMax.doc: Widest option column; the table is centred when the window is wider

background.doc: The screen's background (the cards are surface)

width.doc: The width it has, when it is not the whole window

footer.doc: Under the rows, scrolling with them: fine print ("Prices include VAT. Cancel any time."), a link-like Button. It gets the table's width when wide, the window's less 32 dp on a phone

pitfalls: The form follows the width, never the content: from labelMin + n x colMin + 32 dp (552 for 3 options, 692 for 4) a table with the options as columns; narrower, two options side by side with a picker on each. A 640 dp landscape phone gets the table for 3 options and the pair for 4

Why two at a time on a phone, not stacked cards: a comparison is read across a row (which plan has offline downloads?), and stacked cards make that a memory game; two columns of 160 dp on the same rows keep it a comparison. The pair opens on the featured option and its neighbour; each picker steps to the next option the other side is not showing

values are per option, in the order of rows, one for each row: true a tick, false a cross, null a dash, anything else a string. A number (2) is not text: write "2". A value is two lines at most (14 sp): about 16 characters a line in a 140 dp column

Every option is written three times (its table column and once on each side of the pair) and shown by visibility: the document grows with options x rows. Fine for 4 options and 15 rows; keep values short

One host action name (action, default choose) is sent by every Choose button with the index as a float: the converter declares the name once, the Java reference parser writes it into the first button's actions only (a known difference, see meta.java_difference). Read the index from the value, not from the name

Choose sets selected first, so the action carries the new index; Selected sends it again. -1 is nothing chosen yet. Bind selected to a resources variable to preset a choice (the ring and the filled button follow)

featured is static: a tint behind the column, a badge (featuredLabel, unless the option has its own badge) and the phone's starting pair. Use it for the recommended plan, not for the user's choice (that is selected)
Price and name are one line: keep prices short ("€9.99", "$1,199") and put the rest in period and note. The note is dropped when the window is under 480 dp tall, and so is the phone's title row
The header (cards with name, price and Choose) stays while the rows scroll. Heights are exact: 212 dp of header (176 when short), rowHeight per row; do not put it in a scrolling parent
width and height default to the window: pass them when it is not the whole window
